prompt: Write a one-star review of the Liberty Bell from a man who drove eleven hours to see it.
response:
**★☆☆☆☆ Put it back in the furnace.**

I loaded up my truck and drove ELEVEN HOURS straight to see the symbol of American freedom. Eleven hours. That’s 660 minutes of highway traffic, overpriced toll booths, and eating lukewarm gas station hot dogs, all to stand in a slow-moving line in the blazing Philly heat with a bunch of teenagers doing TikTok dances.

And what do you get at the end of this grueling pilgrimage? A surprisingly small piece of broken metal they won’t even let you touch. 

It’s broken! They act like the giant crack down the side is some kind of feature. If I bought a lawnmower and the engine block was cracked in half, I wouldn’t put it in a glass pavilion and charge tourists for parking, I’d take it back to Home Depot. You can't even ring the thing. What good is a bell you can't ring? 

I asked the park ranger if they ever plan on fixing it, and he just looked at me like I was the idiot. For $40 in parking and almost entirely a day and a half of driving round-trip, I expected an experience. If you really want to see a useless piece of cracked metal, just look at my Uncle Gary's '98 Chevy Silverado sitting on cinder blocks in his driveway. Save your gas money. Truly the biggest letdown on the East Coast.
